biology-map.html.title: Biology Map
transcript: Welcome to Biology Map. See how humans are related to other living things, how much DNA we share, and how DNA, genes, mutations and evolution work.
The tree of life shows forty-three living things, from bacteria to humans. Every branch point is a common ancestor. Let us open the chimpanzee.
Chimpanzees share about ninety-nine percent of our DNA letters, and our lines split about six and a half million years ago. The gold and blue lines show both paths back to that ancestor.
You also see what we both inherited, and what evolved on each line since the split.
Now a distant relative: the banana. We shared an ancestor over one and a half billion years ago.
Sixty percent of banana genes have a human counterpart — but that does not mean sixty percent of our DNA letters match. The tool always says what each number measures.
The ranking compares all the figures side by side.
Tap any branch point to see what evolved there, like the first mammals, with hair and milk.
Drag the time slider to travel back and see the key events in the history of life.
What DNA is: a double helix written with four letters, A, T, G and C. Tap each level to zoom from your body down to a single letter.
Type letters to build a DNA strand. The matching strand appears, because A always pairs with T, and G with C.
Gene expression shows, step by step, how a gene is copied into RNA and translated into a protein.
The codon translator reads real DNA three letters at a time. Here is the start of the insulin gene.
In the mutation lab you can change a real human gene. Try the sickle cell mutation: one letter changes, and one amino acid in haemoglobin changes with it.
Delete a single letter and the whole reading frame shifts — a frameshift that breaks the protein.
The evolution simulator shows natural selection. On dark bark, dark moths are hidden from birds, and in a few dozen generations they take over.
Human diversity follows our ancestors out of Africa to every continent.
Tap a pin to see how a population adapted, like Tibetans living at high altitude with a gene they got from Denisovans.
The facts explain that any two people share about 99.9 percent of their DNA, and that most variation is found within groups, not between them.
Finally, test yourself. Choose a topic and press Generate quiz.
Pick an answer to see the explanation. You can also print a quiz with an answer key.
Now it is your turn. Open Biology Map on MigaBuilder and try it yourself. It is free, and there is nothing to sign up for.

Shape it with the sliders. We make it a little longer and wider.
Deadrise gives the bottom a V, and flare makes the sides lean out.
Add people and a bigger engine. The boat sinks until it displaces its own weight of water, then trims until it balances.
Try the heel test to see how hard the boat pushes itself back upright.
Below the 3D view you get the weight, draft, freeboard, stability and estimated speed, with checks written in plain language.
The lines plan draws the profile, the half-breadth plan and the body plan, ready to download for CAD.
The stability curve shows the righting arm at every angle of heel.
For plywood boats, the panels are unrolled flat so you can cut them from sheets, with station molds and a material list.
Download the panels full size as a DXF file for cutting, and the lines, offsets, 3D model and a printable build sheet from the other tabs.

body-map.html.title: Body Map
transcript: Welcome to Body Map. Learn how every organ, bone, muscle and layer of skin works, what can go wrong with it, and how to keep it healthy.
The map shows the main organs and body parts. Hover over one to see its name, and click to open it. Let us open the heart.
You see what it does, where it is, and how it works, step by step.
Connections show how it works with other parts of the body. The connected parts light up on the map.
Every part lists its common illnesses. Open one to see the signs, the best way to treat it, and how to prevent it. Possible emergencies are clearly marked.
Below that are the best ways to keep it healthy, and some surprising facts.
Use the coloured buttons to show one body system, like digestion, then click any organ in it, like the liver.
The connections map shows how every part works together with the others.
The layer buttons switch between organs, the skeleton, muscles and tendons, and a cut-through view of the skin. Here is the skeleton. Let us open the spine.
Muscles and tendons have a front and a back view. Muscles are red and tendons are white, like the Achilles tendon at the back of the ankle.
The skin layers view shows the outer skin, the dermis and the fat layer, with hair, oil glands and sweat glands. Tap any of them.
Now, what happens when we eat? Open Eating and drinking. The dot follows a meal through the body.
The stomach churns the food with acid, the pancreas and gallbladder add their juices, and the small intestine absorbs the nutrients into the blood.
Switch to a drink to see how water reaches the blood, the kidneys and the bladder.
Tap a card to see which organs handle carbohydrates, fats, caffeine or alcohol.
The Fasting tab shows what happens hour by hour after your last meal. Drag the slider, or pick a fast like sixteen hours.
After about a day, the liver has used up its stored sugar. The body burns more fat and makes ketones, and the bar shows where the energy comes from.
Safety notes explain why you must keep drinking water, and who should not fast without a doctor.
Now test yourself. Choose the whole body, one body system or one body part, and press Generate quiz.
Pick an answer. You get an explanation every time, and your best score is saved.
You can also make your own quiz. Give it a title, choose a body part, and add suggested questions. Then edit them, or write your own.
Play it, save it, print it with an answer key, or copy a link to share it with a class or a friend.
Finally, the daily checklist shows which healthy habits help which parts of your body.
Now it is your turn. Open Body Map on MigaBuilder and try it yourself. It is free, and there is nothing to sign up for.

chemistry-map.html.title: Chemistry Map
transcript: Welcome to Chemistry Map. Explore all one hundred and eighteen elements, see how they combine, and discover what materials they make.
Every element has its own square, coloured by its family. Hover over one for a quick summary.
Open an element, like carbon. You see its atom, with protons and neutrons in the nucleus and electrons in shells.
Then where it is found, what it is used for, and its different forms — carbon can be diamond, graphite or graphene.
It lists the compounds it makes and the materials made with it.
The colour buttons show patterns. Solid, liquid or gas shows each element at the temperature you choose. At room temperature only mercury and bromine are liquid.
Heat it to the surface of the Sun, and almost everything boils.
Electronegativity shows which atoms pull electrons hardest — fluorine, at the top right.
Now mix elements. With this box ticked, tapping the table puts elements in the bowl. Add sodium and chlorine.
The mixer explains the bond — sodium gives an electron to chlorine, an ionic bond — predicts the formula, NaCl, and shows the real compound: table salt.
Try a classic like calcium, carbon and oxygen, which make limestone, chalk and seashells.
Materials shows what the elements build. Tap one, like a lithium-ion battery, and its elements light up in the table.
The formula calculator works out molar mass and what share each element makes up. Here is glucose.
How atoms bond explains atoms, shells, and ionic, covalent and metallic bonds with diagrams.
Search for any use, like battery, to light up every element that is used in batteries.
Finally, test yourself. Choose the elements and question types, then press Generate quiz.
Pick an answer and you get an explanation, with a link to open that element.
Now it is your turn. Open Chemistry Map on MigaBuilder and try it yourself. It is free, and there is nothing to sign up for.

exam-checker.html.title: Exam Checker
transcript: Welcome to Exam Checker. Build an exam, print an answer sheet for every student, drop in photos of all the sheets at once, and download everyone’s marks.
The How to use box at the top lists the six steps. Press Load demo exam to see a finished example with a class of six.
Step one: build the exam. Each question has a type: multiple choice, choose all that apply, true or false, a short answer or an open answer, with its points.
Paste your class list here, one student per line, with their ID and name.
Step two is the answer key. Tap the correct bubble for each question, or read the key from a photo of a filled-in sheet.
Step three: press Print one sheet per student. Every sheet has the student’s name, their ID and a code printed on it.
The code along the bottom edge tells the checker whose sheet it is, so nobody has to type names, and the photos can be in any order.
Step four tests the reader. Photograph a sheet with the correct answers, and the checker compares every answer with your key. Here we use a test photo.
Every answer matches, and it even knows whose sheet it is. Now you are ready to mark the class.
Step five: drop in the photos of all the sheets at once, in any order. Here we add demo photos: they are shuffled, one sheet is photographed twice, and one student is missing.
Every photo went to the right student. The sheet photographed twice was counted only once, and the class list shows who is not marked yet.
Find a student, show only the ones that need checking, or sort by score.
Press Next answer to check. It opens the next student with something for you to look at: a faint mark, two filled bubbles, or a written answer.
Correct answers are circled in green and wrong ones in red. Tap a bubble to fix an answer.
Written answers are shown as pictures. Type what the student wrote, and it is marked automatically.
Step six shows the results: the average, the spread of scores, every student’s answers, and which questions most students missed.
Download everyone’s answers as Excel or CSV, a class report, or printable result slips for each student.
Now it is your turn. Open Exam Checker on MigaBuilder and try it yourself. It is free, and there is nothing to sign up for.
